issues.description: Docs do not say whether `at=` positions the text's cap-height box or the baseline by default; I passed align=('center','center') to be safe and did not verify the exact vertical centring numerically.
No direct query for text bounding box / extents of engraved or embossed text, so centring (0,4) and (0,-8) was only checked visually.

The docs example for engrave/emboss does not show that `at` is the text anchor, so centring on (x, y) requires align=('center','center'). I passed it explicitly. I did not verify whether the default is already centred.

suggestions.suggestion: Add a query for the bbox of faces created by a text feature (e.g. emboss1.end).
State the default vertical alignment of text in the docs.
State the default `align` for text in `cad docs text`.
Add a `cad measure --text` or query that reports the text bounding box and centre, so centring can be checked numerically.
Add a query/measure to report text extents (bbox of engraved/emboss features) so centring and cap height can be verified numerically rather than only by render.
Show the align=('center','center') default behaviour explicitly in the docs example, since centring on `at` depends on it.
